name: Combinatorics: Enumora
subtitle: Combinatorics and Counting
shortDescription: Adaptive combinatorics course: counting, generating functions, Ramsey colourings and partitions with five hands-on labs. Free to use.
longDescription:
Combinatorics: Enumora is an adaptive undergraduate course in enumerative and extremal combinatorics. It teaches you to count carefully, to prove why a count is right, and to bound what is possible.

Sixteen topics build on each other: sum and product rules, permutations and combinations, binomial coefficients and Pascal's triangle, stars and bars, the pigeonhole principle, inclusion-exclusion, derangements, linear recurrences, ordinary generating functions, Catalan numbers, integer partitions and Young diagrams, Stirling and Bell numbers, Burnside counting for necklaces, Ramsey basics, block designs, and Sperner, Erdos-Ko-Rado and Mantel extremal results.

### How It Adapts
Pick the personalised path or the traditional syllabus order and switch any time. The engine on your device tracks mastery of every topic, schedules reviews on a 1, 2, 4, 7 and 14 day rhythm, and tags each wrong answer with the counting error behind it: order counted too much, add or multiply mix-up, overcounting symmetry, a missing inclusion-exclusion term, an off-by-one. Your counting ledger shows which habit to fix next, and the next set is built around it.

### What You Get
- 153 original questions in multiple choice, typed number and true/false forms, each with a free worked solution. Every numerical answer was recomputed by a second method (exhaustive enumeration, dynamic programming or symbolic algebra).
- Five labs: a Pascal triangle explorer with remainder colouring, a generating function series explorer for coins, Fibonacci and partitions, a Young diagram lab with conjugates and hook lengths, a Ramsey colouring game on K5 and K6, and a recurrence solver stepper that walks from the characteristic equation to a closed form.
- Mock exams of 12 verified questions with a timer and review.
- Pop-ups on key ideas that explain them at school level and point to later courses, plus before-and-after course pages.
- Citations to university courses, textbooks and journals that open in a full-width sheet with the licence and a link. All teaching text and problems are original; sources are cited, never copied.
- A-/A+ text size control on every screen, accessibility labels, and a layout designed for both phone and tablet.

Works offline. Your progress stays on your device. The app is free to use with ads shown only at natural breaks after a practice set, never during exams or before a solution. You can earn extra mock exams by choosing to watch a short video, or remove ads with an optional monthly subscription (price shown by the App Store, 7-day free trial for new subscribers; renews monthly until cancelled in Settings, at least 24 hours before the period ends).

Not affiliated with any university or publisher named in the citations.
monetization: Free with ads, optional monthly ad-free
